title: L2: the translator hub IR (docs/TRANSLATOR_DESIGN.md, IR_UNIFICATION.md, L2_BINARY_TYPES.md)
description: One typed tree for every source language and for decompiled binaries. ir.py implements it in Python; the Rust core implements the same schema (serde). A document is a Node, usually a Module or a Unit.

Class.description: a nominal type (a class, interface, enum, struct by name) with its type arguments

SegmentRef.description: which segment a near pointer is relative to, or what a selector names

seg.description: near only: the segment the offset is in

Record.description: explicit layout: offsets fixed, gaps explicit (structures, frames, data segments)

pops.description: argument bytes the callee removes; null = not known

Origin.description: provenance: where in the original binary a node came from

oneOf.description: a statement of a decompiled function: the addresses of the instructions it was made from

Sym.description: what a name refers to, as the source language resolved it

Comment.description: a comment the source carries at this place among the statements (a decompiler's warning): its text, without the delimiters; a back end for the same language writes it where it stands

text.description: the literal as the source spelled it (base, suffix, character escape): a back end for the same language prints it so

name.description: the function (or label) the fragment stands for, as the module's other parts call it

syntax.description: the assembler `asm` is written for (wasm, masm, nasm); with `asm` null, `within` names the fragment that holds its text

within.description: the name of the fragment whose `asm` holds this one's too (a run of functions assembled as one file)

MachineFragment.description: what stays assembly (L2_BINARY_TYPES.md section 7) -- a statement, a member or a whole function: where it came from, its length in bytes, why (hand-written, register-arguments, ...), its text

comments.description: comments written above the declaration (a decompiler's warnings), each as its text

text.description: the function's source as text, where its tree is not yet written (the C a function store holds, which the text passes of source/readable.py read)

MethodDecl.description: kind: method, ctor, static_init, init, or function (a free function: C, a decompiled binary). A calling-convention-carrying fn type rides on sym.type.

header.description: the module's declarations as text (the header its functions' C is compiled with), where they are not yet a tree

Node.description: any node, dispatched on its "node" field (if/then, so validation stays linear)
